chunks: Abi (may Allah have mercy on him) from Sa’d ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Sama’ah from Ibn Mihran from his father from Abi Basir from one of the Imams (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'Which charity is the best?' He replied, 'The effort (sacrifice) of the poor (one with little wealth).'
Did you not hear the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?
And they prefer (others) over themselves, even though poverty may afflict them.
ai.seo_question: What is the most virtuous type of charity in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the spiritual status of the poor by defining the excellence of charity as 'the effort of the straitened one' (juhd al-muqill), emphasizing sincere sacrifice over mere quantity. This concept is deeply rooted in the Quranic account of the Ansar, who, despite their own need, prioritized the Muhajirun, thereby establishing a paradigm of selflessness (ithar) central to Shia ethical teachings. The hadith thus shifts the metric of reward from absolute wealth to the relative degree of deprivation and generosity.
